findings.title: Decision 4 makes the AUTO pew fire a three-round burst when every hold ends, which spec §4.3 rules out
findings.claim: Decision 4 lets an AUTO pew fire every stored third on consecutive on-solution ticks. The pew starts each round full (state.ts L230: `pewCharge: pew ? pewFullCharge(pew) : 0`), and tickPew keeps it full through the 30 s hold. So the AUTO pew's first act in every round is three rounds on ticks h, h+1 and h+2. This is not an edge case. Spec §4.3 states the result it requires: "So it fires each time a third has charged, and it never bursts." Reading that as "no deliberate burst rule" contradicts the spec. The codebase already calls rapid stored-thirds fire a burst: the Hunter's pewBurst, and hunter.ts L123 "after a burst it waits for every third".
findings.evidence: plan L58 (Decision 4), L1197 (`else if (auto.pew && hostile) firePewTrigger`), L1056-1062 (the test pins the 3-round opener via `at.slice(3)`); spec L204-205; state.ts L230; pew.ts L41-44 (pewReady), L86-89 (tickPew to full); hunter.ts L123
findings.why: The spec is fixed and not reopened. As written, every duel opens with an AUTO pew burst at hold end. That changes the opener, the gates and the tuning ladder's baseline.
findings.fix: Use a stateless rule that meets both halves of the sentence. In applyWeaponsInput, AUTO fires when `auto.pew && hostile && (s.pewCharge >= pewFull(def) || s.pewCharge % pewThird(def) < pewGain(state, i))`. That is: the pew is full, or its last tickPew has just completed a third. From full it fires one round; the charge then sits at 2/3 + gain, and the next AUTO round comes when the next third completes, every PEW_TICKS_BY_BARS ticks. The AUTO gains 6/8/12/15 divide 360 exactly, so the modulo test is integer and exact. The simplest alternative is to fire only at a full charge (`pewCharge >= pewFull(def)`), which keeps two thirds in reserve. Record the choice as a corrected Decision 4. Rewrite Task 6's first test to expect one round at hold end, then a gap of PEW_RECHARGE_TICKS between every round, `at.slice(1)` included.

findings.title: Task 4 expects the pew's solution at bearing 40 to be 40×256, but the lead from the muzzle is heading 42
findings.claim: `autoSolution(st, 0, 'pew')` takes its lead from the muzzle, `muzzleForward` = SHIP_RADIUS + 1 = 21 ahead of the centre, not from the centre. The Hunter sits 300 u from the centre on heading 40 (56.25°). Relative to the muzzle it is at (forward 166.7 − 21, lateral 249.4) = 59.7°, which is 42.46 heading steps. nearestHeading returns 42, and 42×256 = 10752 lies inside the ±10922 arc. So the function returns 10752, and `expect(autoSolution(st, 0, 'pew')).toBe(40 * 256)` fails. The bearing-6 cases still pass: the muzzle-relative angle is 6.45 steps, which rounds to 6.
findings.evidence: plan L615-617; pew.ts L67-70 (pewMuzzle), L150-156 (pewLead from the muzzle); defs.ts L99 (`muzzleForward: SHIP_RADIUS + 1`); tuning.ts L38 (SHIP_RADIUS 20); lead.ts L35-43 (nearestHeading)
findings.why: A test written in the plan cannot pass. Task 4 Step 7 expects w4Turret to PASS.
findings.fix: Assert against the sim's own lead: `const e = st.ships[1]!; expect(autoSolution(st, 0, 'pew')).toBe(turretOffset(0, pewLead(st, 0, e.x, e.y, 0, 0)))`, which is 42 × 256. Or pin `42 * 256` with a comment on the muzzle parallax. Keep the `gun` null assertion: 10752 is outside ±5461.

findings.title: Task 6 turns every AUTO-trigger test red, including Task 4's own, with no rewrite named
findings.claim:
After Task 6, a turret gun in AUTO ignores `gunHeld`, and every round starts in AUTO. These tests drive the Hound's autocannon with the held trigger in AUTO, and Task 6 Step 6 expects them to PASS:
- Task 4's 'a pew round and an autocannon round leave along them'. It calls `tickGun(st, 0, { ...IDLE_INPUT, gunHeld: true })` and then dereferences `st.rounds.find(...)!`, so it throws.
- All five `it`s of W-4a's tests/w4Autocannon.test.ts, which use `TRIGGER` on a default-AUTO Hound.
- W-4a's w4PewFire case 'on the Hound gunHeld fires the autocannon only with weaponSel 1'.
Task 6 Step 4 names only w4PewFire's admission test. Setting MAN is not a drop-in fix either: MAN switches to the MAN interval row (8/7/5/4), so W-4a's 10/8/6/5 assertions still fail.
findings.why: The tests go red with no rule. The executor will either set MAN everywhere, which breaks the AUTO-row intervals, or weaken the tests.
findings.fix:
Name the kind (a) rewrites in Task 6, citing W-4 spec §4.3:
- w4Autocannon: the interval, rounds-along-aim, cooldown and six-hits tests call `tickGun(st, 0, IDLE_INPUT, true)`, which is AUTO on solution with the AUTO rows. The heats-and-locks test sets `s.gunsManual = true` and keeps TRIGGER, because only MAN can lock. The 0-bar case uses `auto = true` too.
- Task 4's round test sets `s.gunsManual = true` before `tickGun`, or passes `auto = true`.
- w4PewFire's gunHeld case sets `gunsManual = true`, or is deleted as superseded by Task 6's w4Manual case, named in the commit.
List all three files in Task 6's Files and commit.

findings.title: Task 5 gates LMB and gunHeld on MAN and so turns W-4a's runtime and online tests red; Step 9 says they pass
findings.claim:
Task 5 makes both runtimes send `pewFire` and `gunHeld` only in MAN, and every round starts in AUTO. Several W-4a tests assert the old behaviour on a fresh rig:
- w4Runtime 'LMB: pewFire with pew pew selected …' expects `[sys.pewShots, statuses] = [1, ['applied']]` after a click.
- w4Runtime 'the held trigger sends gunHeld only with the autocannon selected, and a dead trigger refuses NO POWER' expects `gunHeld` true and the NO POWER refusal.
- The onlineDuelSession Hound case (1) expects `{ weaponSel: 1, gunHeld: true }`, and case (2) expects a `pewFire` and NO CHARGE.
Task 5 lists those files only for renames, and Step 9 expects all PASS.
findings.why: The tests go red with no rule. The fallout rule requires each to be classified and rewritten, not left to whoever executes.
findings.fix: In Task 5, name these as kind (a) rewrites (W-4 spec §4.3, §9). Each gets `r.press('weaponMode'); r.tick();` online, or a Z key down/up and a pump, before its existing MAN assertions. The new W-4b `it`s keep the AUTO negatives. Add the files to Step 9's run list and the commit.

findings.title: Task 7 adds `turret` to createDuelRuntime's returned literal but not to the `DuelRuntime` interface, so tsc fails
findings.claim: `createDuelRuntime(deps): DuelRuntime` returns an object literal directly. TypeScript's excess-property check rejects any member that `DuelRuntime` does not declare, and the interface lists every returned member (thrMille L250, takeRefusals L252). Task 7 adds `turret: (slot: 0 | 1) => …` only to the literal and to `DuelViewSource`.
findings.evidence: plan L1382; runtime.ts L204-254 (interface DuelRuntime), L269, L559
findings.why: Task 7 Step 5 `npx tsc -b` fails with TS2353. W-4a's `weaponSel` addition has the same shape, so the fix is the same.
findings.fix: In Task 7 Step 4, also add `/** W-4 spec §11: gun slot's turret offset (the sim's; no lag locally). */ turret(slot: 0 | 1): number;` to `interface DuelRuntime` in runtime.ts, beside W-4a's `weaponSel` if W-4a added it there.

findings.title: The W-4b/W-4c seam: W-4c anchors on `turret()`, a void-returning MAN branch and a trigger text that W-4b does not leave
findings.claim:
W-4c's anchors do not match the shapes W-4b leaves:
1. W-4c greps for `turret()` in onlineSource.ts and stops if it is missing (W-4c L128-129). It calls `source.turret()` with no argument (L866), and adds its flight gate to onlineSource's own conjunction (L948). W-4b defines `turret(slot: 0 | 1)`, with the k = 0 gates inside `predictTurret` in weaponsSeat.ts. So the grep fails, `turret()` fails tsc, and the conjunction W-4c names does not exist. W-4c never mentions `predictTurret`.
2. W-4c inserts `if (sys.gunsManual && manualTorpedoFlying(state, i)) return;` as the MAN branch's first statement (L569). In W-4b the MAN branch sits inside the `for` over both guns, in a function returning `AutoOnSolution`, so a bare `return;` fails tsc. It must be `continue`, or `return out`.
3. W-4c L946 anchors on `sessionHeld(k, d, me, steer, { sel: weaponSel, trigger: requests.triggerHeld() })`. W-4a's text is `trigger: triggerNow()` (W-4a L2191), and W-4b Task 5 Step 6 changes it to `trigger: triggerNow() && (…), aim: reticleNow() ?? -1`.
findings.why: W-4c consumes these names. As written, W-4c's first check stops the run, and two of its edits do not compile or do not match.

findings.title: Task 10: a kept rung turns pinned tests red with no rule, and the `1 | 2` knob may not compile
findings.claim:
Three gaps in Task 10:
- Keeping rung 2 (`AUTOCANNON_AUTO_RANGE` 450) breaks W-4a's w4Loadout pin, `[…, AUTOCANNON_AUTO_RANGE, …]` toEqual `[…, 600, 800]`.
- Keeping rung 4 breaks Task 6's 'its first seated tick sends shipPower … then weaponPower Autocannon +1 … weaponPower [1, 1, 1]'. Task 10 updates only w4Loadout's hitsPerHull destructuring.
- `export const HOUND_GUNNER_AUTOCANNON_BARS: 1 | 2 = 1;` followed by `HOUND_GUNNER_AUTOCANNON_BARS === 2` is very likely rejected. TypeScript narrows a const by its initialiser, so the comparison of `1` with `2` fails with TS2367 at Step 1's `npx tsc -b`.
findings.why: Step 4 expects the fences and gates green, and the ladder's no-op step must compile.
findings.fix: Add a rule to Task 10 Step 3: for the setting kept, update the tests it pins. Rung 2 changes the w4Loadout pin to `AUTOCANNON_AUTO_RANGE`'s new value with a `// W-4b ladder: was 600` note. Rung 4 makes the first-tick test read the four commands and `[0, 2, 1]`. Both are kind (a), citing spec §12, and go in the commit. Declare the knob as `export const HOUND_GUNNER_AUTOCANNON_BARS = 1 as 1 | 2;` (or type it `number`) so the comparison type-checks.

findings.title: Outline test bodies and 'check at execution' notes are left for the executor
findings.claim: Task 8's six `it`s have comment-only bodies. An empty `it` passes, so Step 2's "Expected: FAIL" cannot happen, and one comment is garbled ("16384 / 4 (a quarter of the arc... use 2731)"). Tasks 5, 7 and 9 give their rig cases only in prose. Task 3 L470 leaves "check the noop's status string" to the executor; the code already answers it. `result(e, undefined, 'noop')` yields status `'noop'` (step.ts L317, L322), so Task 3's `toMatchObject({ status: 'noop' })` is right as written.
findings.why: The plan's own placeholder rule and the brief both count outlines as defects. Outline bodies also break TDD.

findings.title: The self-review's note on W-4a's trigger closure is stale, and Task 5 quotes a placeholder instead of W-4a's text
findings.claim: W-4a already reads the online trigger through `const triggerNow = (): boolean => requests.triggerHeld()` and calls `sessionHeld(k, d, me, steer, { sel: weaponSel, trigger: triggerNow() })`. The local runtime reads `deps.triggerHeld?.()`. Task 5 Step 6 quotes `trigger: <the trigger closure>()`, and the self-review says W-4a calls `requests.triggerHeld()` inside play and pump.
findings.why: The rule is to match every edit by the quoted text; a placeholder quote invites a mismatch.
findings.fix: Quote W-4a's exact line, `sessionHeld(k, d, me, steer, { sel: weaponSel, trigger: triggerNow() })`. Drop the conditional in Step 3 and the stale self-review bullet.
